title: Rounding bounds permit both signs of the mean ENSO duration difference in two ERSSTv5 tables for 1950-2025
abstract: We tested how one-decimal rounding can change complete cold and warm run lengths in NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 ONI and RONI for 1950-2025. We assumed nearest-tenth rounding and allowed either threshold label at each displayed threshold-equal value, with no joint constraints on hidden values. At a 0.5 C threshold and a five-season minimum, the exact cold minus warm mean length bounds were -0.77 to +4.29 overlapping seasons for ONI and -1.79 to +2.85 for RONI. The inclusive displayed-value estimates were +2.63 and +0.55 seasons. Both signs were also feasible at thresholds of 0.4 and 0.6 C. A block enumeration method and an independent streaming method agreed on all feasible counts and sum extrema. These bounds show numerical sensitivity under the stated observation model. They are not confidence intervals, and they do not show that a sign reversal is physically likely. Hidden joint constraints, source revisions, record edges and the short record limit interpretation. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an audit and a figure are included; source records remain external.

display.caption: Exact duration difference bounds under the nearest-tenth rounding model. These are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Reproduces its complete-run point estimates on the same snapshots; tests its stated rounding limitation with exact bounds and new code.
Threshold continuity evidence motivates the distinction between annual returns and contiguous runs.
